svg.title: Fabric Data Factory: Pipeline Runs, Triggers, and Copy Paths
svg.desc: An architecture diagram showing the three trigger paths (on-demand, schedule, storage event) converging on a pipeline run, the three parallelism levels within a Copy activity, and the lighter-weight Copy job and Mirroring alternatives.
svg.text: Fabric Data Factory — Pipeline Runs, Triggers & Ingestion Paths
Trigger Paths (Manual · Schedule · Eventstream) ➔ Orchestration & 3 Parallelism Levers ➔ Copy Job & Mirroring
PHASE 1: THE THREE PIPELINE TRIGGER INGESTION PATHS

g.title: On-demand run — A manual pipeline run started from the editor.
g.text: On-Demand Manual Run
Ad-hoc execution from the pipeline canvas editor
• Parameter values supplied dynamically at invocation time
• Ideal for test runs, validation, and ad-hoc backfill execution
⚠️ Operational Gap: Failure email alerts do NOT fire for on-demand runs

g.title: Time-based schedule — Up to 20 schedules per pipeline, each with its own cadence, requiring a start and end date.
g.text: Time-Based Schedule Trigger
Bounded recurrence with multi-cadence support
• Up to 20 independent schedules per single pipeline definition
• Mandatory bounded range: Start date AND End date required for every schedule
• Supports static parameters or variable-library references
⚠️ Silent Fallback Trap: Parameter names must match exactly or default values apply

g.title: Storage event trigger — A file/table event fires the pipeline via eventstream and Data Activator plumbing.
g.text: Storage Event Trigger (Eventstream + Reflex)
Underlying Fabric RTI event-driven plumbing
• Provisions an Eventstream + Data Activator Reflex alert in the workspace
• Subscribes to OneLake or Azure Blob file-created / table-updated events
• Filters on CloudEvents Subject field for file names and paths
Expression Syntax: @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName (null-safe for manual tests)

g.title: Pipeline run (orchestration layer) — The started run executes the pipeline's chained activities — Copy, notebooks, stored procedures, conditionals.
g.text: Pipeline Run: Unified Orchestration Layer
Visual control flow & activity dependency management
Lookup / Meta
Read Watermark
Copy Activity
Scale-Out Ingest
Spark / Notebook
Delta Transforms
Stored Proc
Update Watermark
• Control flow constructs: ForEach loops, If-Condition, Until, Switch
• Chains Fabric Notebooks, Spark Job Definitions, Stored Procedures & dbt
• Code-first teams can author Python DAGs via Apache Airflow orchestration
Monitoring & Observability:
Track duration, activity status, rows read/written, and retry counters in Fabric Monitor Hub

svg.text: PHASE 2: COPY SCALE-OUT LEVERS & LIGHTWEIGHT PRIMITIVES

g.title: Copy activity — Fully customizable data movement inside a pipeline, with three independent parallelism levers.
g.text: Copy Activity — Three Independent Parallelism Levers
Serverless data movement with multi-tier compute & thread controls
LEVER 1
Control-Flow Concurrency (ForEach Fan-Out)
• Launches multiple Copy activities concurrently across partitions or table batches.
• Scales pipeline throughput horizontally across distinct compute workers.
LEVER 2
Intelligent Throughput Optimization (ITO Compute Sizing)
• Presets: Auto · Standard · Balanced · Maximum, or explicit numeric value (4 to 256).
• Directs the underlying CPU, memory, and network provisioned for this activity.
LEVER 3
Degree of Copy Parallelism (Thread-Level Concurrency)
• Internal reader/writer threads working in parallel within a single copy activity.
• Cap threads against fragile on-prem or rate-limited source systems.
Orthogonal Tuning Principle:
All three levers operate independently. Default is dynamic service auto-tuning.

g.title: Copy job & Mirroring — Two lighter-weight data-movement primitives that bypass a full pipeline: Copy job's built-in delivery modes, and Mirroring's continuous database replication.
g.text: Standalone Ingestion: Copy Job & Mirroring
Lightweight primitives bypassing full pipeline orchestration
Copy Job (Built-in Modes):
• Bulk Load: One-time historical movement
• Incremental: Delta append sync
• CDC Replication: Multi-table sync
0 pipeline overhead for simple copy
Database Mirroring:
• Near-real-time operational DB replica
• Replicates Azure SQL, Cosmos, Snowflake
• Continuous Delta sync into OneLake
Direct Lake queryable instantly

g.aria-label: Activator rule invokes Copy job directly
g.title: Activator rule invokes Copy job directly — GA: an Activator rule condition triggers a Copy job as its action, with no pipeline in between.
g.text: GA Pattern: Data Activator Direct Rule Invocation
Event-driven Copy Job execution with 0 pipeline middleware
• Fabric Activator directly invokes a Copy Job as a rule action upon business events
• Replaces rigid polling schedules with pure event-driven ingestion triggers
• Eliminates compute waste from empty scheduled runs and schedule sprawl
Architectural Benefit: Removes intermediate pipeline wrapper for pure event data movement

g.aria-label: Trap: tuning past the real bottleneck
g.title: Trap: tuning past the real bottleneck — Throughput is bounded by the minimum of source, destination, and network capacity — tuning can't exceed it.
g.text: CRITICAL TRAP 1
Tuning Past the True Bottleneck Adds Cost Without Speed
• Throughput = min(Source IOPS, Destination Write Capacity, Network Bandwidth).
• Setting ITO to "Maximum" against a throttled REST API or source DB yields 0 gain.
Remedy: Profile source read/network bottlenecks in Monitor Hub before scaling ITO.

g.aria-label: Trap: private links block Warehouse/Eventhouse Copy targets
g.title: Trap: private links block Warehouse/Eventhouse Copy targets — Copy activity to/from Warehouse, and Copy to Eventhouse, are unsupported under private-link configurations.
g.text: CRITICAL TRAP 2
Private Links Block Direct Warehouse & Eventhouse Copy
• Copy activity to/from Warehouse is unsupported under private-link security.
• Direct Copy to Eventhouse is unsupported at tenant- and workspace-level scopes.
Remedy: Land data into Lakehouse Delta first, then cross-query into Warehouse.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Data Factory Architecture Specs.
